contract.title: Laminar pressure drop in a 5 mm x 0.3 m 2D water channel at Um=0.02 m/s
contract.requested_prompt: Water at 20 C flows through a 2D channel of height 5 mm and length 0.3 m at a mean velocity of 0.02 m/s. What is the pressure drop, and how does it compare with the analytic laminar value?

objectives.description: A healthy, mesh-resolved steady laminar solution is reached within budget (solver/mesh/case-integrity baseline checks are injected automatically at freeze; these cover the geometry- and field-specific health claims beyond that baseline).
The SIMPLE iteration reaches a stationary (residual-converged) state before the horizon, and the reported quantities are read from that stationary window.

The measured pressure drop in the fully-developed core of the channel (x = 0.05-0.25 m, beyond the ~0.02 m laminar entrance length) matches the analytic plane-Poiseuille gradient dp/dx = 12 mu Um / H^2.
The total inlet-to-outlet pressure drop (which also includes entrance-region excess loss) is reported and is consistent in magnitude with the fully-developed analytic total.

checks.rationale: The channel is planar: exactly two solution directions (x, y).
Realized cell count must equal the specified 150x60x1 block layout (9000 cells).
Inlet, outlet, walls, and the spanwise empty patch must exist.
A cyclic patch would turn this into a different (periodic) problem.
The spanwise (z) direction must be declared empty for the 2D case.
With the outlet referenced at p=0 and a monotonically falling pressure, kinematic pressure must stay non-negative everywhere in this unidirectional laminar flow.
The reported window_mean statistics must be computed from a window that is at least as long as the declared stationarity window (50 iterations), so they are not contaminated by the startup transient.
SIMPLE's residualControl block (p<1e-8, U<1e-9) must report convergence, confirming the steady solution has settled rather than merely exhausting the iteration budget.

In the fully-developed core (x=0.05-0.25 m, well beyond the ~0.0199 m laminar entrance length for Re~100), the measured pressure gradient must match the analytic plane-Poiseuille formula dp/dx = 12*mu*Um/H^2 (reference 1.92421 Pa over 0.2 m) to within 5%, a bound that covers the discretization error of a 150x60 orthogonal mesh at this Re without masking a genuine defect.

The inlet-to-outlet drop (reference 2.88632 Pa for the fully-developed formula over the full 0.3 m) also carries an entrance-region excess loss bounded by a few multiples of the dynamic pressure 0.5*rho*Um^2 (0.1996 Pa, ~6.9% of the analytic total) plus outlet-BC discretization; 25% accommodates this physically-expected excess without masking a genuine solver defect.

assumptions.justification: Standard density of liquid water at 20 C, 1 atm (e.g. NIST/CRC tables, rho(20C)=998.2 kg/m^3).
Standard kinematic viscosity of liquid water at 20 C (nu=1.004e-6 m^2/s, i.e. dynamic viscosity mu=1.0016e-3 Pa s).

assumptions.value: 2D planar channel, H=0.005 m, L=0.3 m
assumptions.justification: Directly stated in the request (channel height 5 mm, length 0.3 m, 2D).

assumptions.value: uniform (plug) inlet at the stated mean velocity 0.02 m/s
assumptions.justification: The request gives only a mean velocity with no inlet profile; a uniform inlet is the standard choice and lets the laminar entrance region develop naturally inside the domain (entrance length ~0.02 m << 0.3 m domain length).

Re~100 is far below the plane-channel transitional Reynolds number (~2300), so a laminar (not RAS/LES) model is the physically correct and budget-cheapest choice; this is not separately gated by a CFD-measured metric but follows directly from the stated geometry and velocity.

contract.reference: Analytic reference: fully-developed plane (2D) Poiseuille flow between parallel plates, dp/dx = 12*mu*Um/H^2 (e.g. F.M. White, Viscous Fluid Flow, 3rd ed., Sec. 3-2; equivalently Fox, McDonald & Pritchard, Introduction to Fluid Mechanics, laminar flow between parallel plates). Water properties at 20 C, 1 atm (rho=998.2 kg/m^3, nu=1.004e-6 m^2/s) from standard tables (NIST WebBook / CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics).
limitations: Single-mesh verification on a 150x60 orthogonal grid; no formal mesh-independence (GCI) study was performed.

The analytic reference (dp/dx = 12 mu Um / H^2) is the fully-developed plane-Poiseuille solution; it does not include the entrance-region excess pressure loss, which is why the full inlet-to-outlet comparison uses a looser tolerance than the core-region comparison.
Water properties are standard 20 C table values, not independently re-derived from an equation of state.
